Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we're all aligned. I've included Rishi (AE) and Neha (Solutions Engineer) on this thread to coordinate the technical side.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for customer support summarization pipeline (latency < 150ms p50, cost target <$0.002/token, and maintain ROUGE-L >= 0.6 vs current baseline).
- Scope: 2-week trial using sample dataset (support tickets) and integration with Acme's ingestion pipeline.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent sessions with avg response time < 300ms for 1k token prompts
  - Quality: human-eval pass rate >= 80% on supplied prompt set
  - Operational: streaming responses and tool-calling (knowledge-base lookup) working end-to-end

Proposed evaluation plan + timeline
1) Week 0 (this week): sign PO and share dataset + service account for testing (read-only S3)
2) Week 1: Integration: SDK install, basic generate API + streaming, validate auth and network
3) Week 2: Run evals (prompt set), tune batch/cache settings, quantify cost/latency
4) End of Week 2: Demo results + go/no-go decision

Owners / asks
- Acme: provide sample dataset + service account; two engineering contacts for integration. (Action: Alex/Priya)
- Redwood: provide integration guide, SDK snippets, sample webhook config, and a small support window for onboarding (Neha). (Action: Neha + Marissa)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming Priya as the primary eng contact. Below is a compact integration plan and sample code to get you started. I attached the longer integration guide and the success-criteria spreadsheet to this thread.

Integration plan (high-level)
1) Auth & Networking
- We will create a read-only API key / service account scoped to the POC. Support both API key header and short-lived OAuth tokens for private deployments.
- If Acme requires VPC-peering or private endpoints, we can coordinate with infra; for this POC we recommend testing over secured HTTPS endpoints.

2) SDKs & Endpoints
- SDKs supported: Node (npm package @redwood/inference), Python (pip redwood-inference).
- Core routes: POST /v1/generate (sync), POST /v1/stream (streaming SSE/WebSocket), POST /v1/toolcalls (tool invocation webhook helper).
- Example minimal requests:
  - Node (generate):
    const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
    const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt: 'Summarize ticket #123', max_tokens: 512 });

  - Node (streaming SSE):
    // using the SDK helper which returns an EventSource-like stream
    const stream = client.stream({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt: 'Summarize ticket #123' });
    stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.text));

  - Curl (tool call example):
    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcalls \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"tool": "kb_lookup", "input": {"query": "error 502 on checkout"}, "callback_url": "https://acme-callback.example.com/kb"}'

3) Tool-calling / Webhook flow
- Redwood will send a POST to your callback_url with payload: {"id": "call-12345", "tool": "kb_lookup", "input": {...}}. Your service should respond within 10s with {"id":"call-12345","result": {...}}. If no response, Redwood will fallback to the primary model path (we can tune retry policy).

4) Streaming & Latency optimizations
- We recommend 64-token chunks for streaming to balance latency and network overhead.
- Use our SDK's prefix/KV cache options for repeated context to reduce token costs. We'll provide suggested batching config after we see your traffic pattern.

5) Instrumentation & Evals
- We'll provide an eval harness (script + prompt set) to run against the model and produce ROUGE/L scores. We'll also instrument token-level latency and cost reporting via the Console dashboard.

Attachments included:
- redwood-sdk-integration.md (detailed steps + code samples)
- acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (success criteria + measurement plan)
- sample-webhook-config.json (example callback endpoints + auth)

Notes / security
- Webhook auth: we support HMAC signatures on callbacks and mutual TLS if required.
- Data retention: by default POC logs retained for 30 days; we can adjust per contract.
